# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

content.text:
I've mapped it. The app assumes in its core logic that every job has both apps, so this isn't only a change to the CTA. [Certain] Every point below comes from code I read.

**What breaks if the server sends a job without `learn_app` / `deliver_app`**
1. **Parsing fails.** `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:285-293`) calls `json.getJSONObject(META_LEARN_APP)` and the deliver equivalent. Those calls throw when the key is missing, so the job never reaches the device. `learn_progress` is required in the same way.
2. **Storage crashes.** `JobStoreManager.java:71-74, 278-318` writes and deletes both app records and learn modules unconditionally.
3. **Job status depends on learn progress.** `fromJson` (`:296-302`) sets LEARNING or DELIVERING from `getLearningPercentComplete`. That calls `passedAssessment()`, which reads `getLearnAppInfo().getPassingScore()` (`:657`). With no learn app, this crashes. Even with a null guard, the job could never leave AVAILABLE.
4. **About ten screens read app info directly.**
   - The job list checks whether each app is installed (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment.kt:151-152, 281`).
   - Intro and modules read `learnAppInfo.learnModules` (`ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt:158`, `ConnectLearnModulesBottomSheet.kt:40`).
   - Learn progress checks install state (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment.kt:120`, `ConnectLearnProgressView.kt:194`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView.kt:104`).
   - Delivery home does the same (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment.kt:139, 185`).
5. **All CTAs go through one function.** `BaseConnectFragment.launchApp()` (`:439`) installs or launches the app. It's called from intro (after the start-learning API call), learn progress (including after claim), delivery home, the dashboard, and delivery "more". This is where the "open messaging" branch would go.
6. **Notifications.** Session-endpoint push notifications resolve an app ID per opportunity (`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity`, `FirebaseMessagingUtil.java:383`). Without apps, those would fail. Other notification types probably need checking too. [Likely]

**A gap on the messaging side**
`ConnectMessagingChannelRecord` has no field linking a channel to an opportunity. It only has `channel_source` and `channel_name`. So today the CTA can't open a specific conversation, only the channel list. [Certain] about the missing field; [Guessing] whether the server can add one.

**The question that shapes everything else**
On the learn and deliver screens, the progress bars, modules, assessment, and visit counts all come from activity in CommCare apps. If no app is involved, those screens have nothing to show unless something else supplies the data.

In this new opportunity type, what moves a worker from learning to delivering, and where do completed learning and delivery visits get recorded?

content.text:
You're partly right. The progress numbers come from the API. The module list, assessment, and passing score don't: they come from the `learn_app` object in that same payload, which is the thing that's going away.

[Certain] Here's where each piece comes from on the client:
- **Learn progress** (`completed_modules` / `total_modules`) and **delivery progress** (`deliver_progress`, plus the deliveries and payments APIs) come from the API. They don't depend on whether the app is installed.
- **The module list** on the Intro card and the modules sheet comes from `learn_app.learn_modules` (`ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt:158`).
- **The assessment passing score** comes from `learn_app.passing_score` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:657`).
- **Install state** is a local device check, used by the job list, delivery home, and the learn views.

**Your flow, as I understand it:** Intro (new opportunity) → Claim on the Intro page → job goes straight to DELIVERING → Delivery Home, whose CTA opens messaging. There's no learning phase at all. The channel ID will come later in the opportunity config; until then the CTA opens the channel list. [Guessing] on that interim behaviour.

**What this flow changes, beyond the null-safety work from before:**
1. **Status falls back after claiming. This is the main problem.** `ConnectRepository.kt:129` sets DELIVERING locally after a successful claim. But on the next sync, `fromJson` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:296-302`) recomputes status, and DELIVERING requires learning progress above 0. With no learn app, progress is 0, so a claimed job reverts to AVAILABLE and the worker lands back on Intro. For this opportunity type, the rule needs to become "claimed means delivering."
2. **The Intro CTA changes from start-learning to claim.** Today it calls `startLearning`, sets LEARNING, then `launchApp(isLearning = true)` (`ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt:104-126`). It would call the claim API instead and go to Delivery Home. The claim call and its observer currently live in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`, so Intro would need its own.
3. **Intro has to drop the learn-modules card**, or it shows 0 modules and 0 hours.
4. **"Revisit learning"** in `ConnectDeliveryMoreFragment.kt:48` needs to be hidden.
5. **Delivery Home's CTA** goes to messaging instead of `launchApp`. So does the "launch deliver app" action on the dashboard and the "more" screen.
6. **The claim API on the server** must allow claiming with no learning completed. I haven't checked the server code. [Guessing]

What's wrong or missing in that flow?

Also, should the app recognise this opportunity type from an explicit flag in the opportunity API (an opportunity type field, say), or just from `learn_app` and `deliver_app` being absent?

1. After a claim, server would return the status as delivery and we should respect that. Mostly we want to respect server Opp status everywhere and not make decisions locally. 3. drop the cards entirely 6. right

content.text:
The client doesn't read an opportunity status from the server today, so "respect server status" is a new contract with the server, not an existing one we can just honour. [Certain] `ConnectJobRecord.status` is stored under the `status` key, but `fromJson` never reads it. It always works the status out locally from learn progress and `claim` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:296-302`). The local overrides at `ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt:120` and `ConnectRepository.kt:129` are also local decisions. So this depends on the opportunity API sending a status value (available / learning / delivering, or similar). I haven't checked whether the server already sends one.

Noted:
- **3:** Intro drops the learn cards entirely for this type.
- **6:** The server's claim endpoint must allow claiming without any learning.

You said "everywhere," and that matters for scope. Applied only to the new type, server status is a contained change. Applied to all opportunities, it changes how existing learn/deliver jobs move between states. The local overrides after start-learning and claim would go away or become refresh-from-server. Older server versions or cached jobs without the field would need a fallback.

Should server-driven status apply only to this new no-app opportunity type, or replace the local status logic for every opportunity?
discard my statement, I didn't realise we don't get status from server but figure it out locally.

Understood. Status stays worked out on the device, so for this opportunity type the rule needs a new branch: **claimed means DELIVERING**, regardless of learn progress. Without it, a claimed job reverts to AVAILABLE on the next sync (`ConnectJobRecord.java:296-302`).

Here's the state handling for the no-app type, as I understand it:
- **Unclaimed** → AVAILABLE or AVAILABLE_NEW, as today. The job list shows it under new opportunities, and tapping it opens Intro.
- **Claim on Intro** → calls the existing claim API, sets DELIVERING locally (same as `ConnectRepository.kt:129` already does), and navigates to Delivery Home.
- **Next sync** → `fromJson` sees `claim` present and keeps DELIVERING because the job has no learn app.
- **LEARNING is never used** for this type, so the learn progress screen and the "revisit learning" entry are unreachable.
- **Expired or inactive** → the existing `isFinished()` handling applies unchanged. [Guessing] that finished no-app jobs should look the same in the list as other finished jobs.

What's wrong or missing there?

One question is still open from before: should the app recognise this opportunity type from an explicit field in the opportunity API, or just from `learn_app` and `deliver_app` being absent or null?
we will need to add  a new field on the Opportunity model called delivery_type which will be say "messaging" for this opportunity type

A new persisted field on `ConnectJobRecord` means a Connect DB migration. That's the riskiest mechanical part of this change, so it's worth planning for up front. [Certain] `ConnectJobRecord` is persisted, and adding a `@Persisting` field needs a DB version bump, a `ConnectJobRecordV<N>` snapshot, and an upgrade step, following the existing V2…V21 pattern.

The data model, as I understand it:
- **`delivery_type`** is a new string on the opportunity API. `"messaging"` means the no-app type. If it's absent or has any other value, the job is treated as today's learn/deliver type, so older servers and existing cached jobs keep working. [Guessing] on the default; tell me if the server will always send it.

# Messaging-delivery opportunities (no learn or deliver app)

## Intent

Connect is adding a new kind of opportunity that has no CommCare app at all: no learn app and no
deliver app. The worker reads the Intro page, claims the opportunity, and from then on works through
PersonalID messaging. The Connect pages still exist, but nothing on them installs or launches a
CommCare app; the primary CTA opens messaging instead.

Today the mobile app assumes every opportunity has both apps. Parsing, storage, status derivation,
and most Connect screens dereference `learnAppInfo` / `deliveryAppInfo` unconditionally, so an
opportunity without them either fails to parse or crashes.

## Goals

- Opportunities with `delivery_type = "messaging"` parse, store, and display without crashing.
- Flow: job list → Intro → **Claim** on Intro → status DELIVERING → Delivery Home, whose CTA opens
  PersonalID messaging.
- The status stays DELIVERING across syncs after claim.
- Existing learn/deliver opportunities behave exactly as today.

## Non-goals

- Opening a specific messaging channel. The server will later add a channel id to the opportunity
  config; until then the CTA opens the messaging channel list.
- Server-driven opportunity status. Status remains derived on the device.
- Server changes (the claim endpoint accepting a claim with no learning, sending `delivery_type`).
  These are prerequisites owned by the server team.

## Anti-goals

- Inferring the type from `learn_app` / `deliver_app` being null. The type comes only from
  `delivery_type`.
- Any regression in the existing learn → claim → deliver flow, including for jobs cached before the
  upgrade.

## Server contract

On the opportunity list API, for a messaging opportunity:

- `delivery_type`: new string field. `"messaging"` marks this type. Absent or any other value means
  the existing learn/deliver type (older servers, existing cached jobs).
- `learn_app`: `null`.
- `deliver_app`: `null`.
- `learn_progress`: still present; parsed as today.

Other APIs:

- Learn progress API: the client must never call it for a job whose `learnAppInfo` is null.
- Claim API: called from Intro; the server accepts it with no learning completed.
- Delivery progress, deliveries, and payments APIs: unchanged.

## Design

### Data model and storage

- Add a persisted `deliveryType` field to `ConnectJobRecord` (`delivery_type`), plus a single
  predicate on the record (e.g. `isMessagingDelivery()`). Every branch below checks this predicate.
- Bump `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` (currently 30), add the `ConnectJobRecordV<N>` snapshot, and add an
  upgrade step in `ConnectDatabaseUpgrader` that backfills existing rows with the default type.
  Prior migrations that targeted `ConnectJobRecord.class` must be retargeted to the new snapshot,
  following the existing V2…V21 pattern.
- `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson`: read `learn_app` and `deliver_app` as nullable; both app records stay
  null when the JSON value is null.
- `JobStoreManager` (store and delete paths, learn module writes) and
  `ConnectJobUtils` (`getCompositeJob` module attach, `getAppIdForOpportunity`) skip absent app
  records instead of dereferencing them.

### Status

Status stays derived locally in `fromJson`. Add a branch: for a messaging job, `claim` present →
`STATUS_DELIVERING`; otherwise `STATUS_AVAILABLE`. A messaging job never enters `STATUS_LEARNING`.

`passedAssessment()` reads `learnAppInfo.passingScore`, so it must not run for jobs without a learn
app.

### Screens

| Screen | Change for messaging jobs |
|---|---|
| Job list (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment`) | No app-installed checks; no app record lookup for last-accessed date. |
| Intro (`ConnectJobIntroFragment`) | CTA claims the job instead of start-learning. On success, set DELIVERING locally (as `ConnectRepository.claimJob` already does) and navigate to Delivery Home. Learn cards are dropped entirely. |
| Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`) | CTA opens messaging via `ConnectNavHelper.goToMessaging` (no channel id for now). No install-state checks. Skip `loadLearningProgress`. |
| Delivery dashboard / more | Task open and "launch deliver app" actions don't call `launchApp`; "revisit learning" is hidden. |
| `ConnectActivity.handleInfoRedirect` | A non-delivering messaging job routes to Intro, not the learn progress screen. |

The claim call and its observer currently live in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`; Intro needs
the same claim handling (loading, error, success) on its own ViewModel.

### Learn progress API guard

Guard inside `ConnectRepository.getLearningProgress`: if `learnAppInfo` is null, don't make the call.
This covers Delivery Home's `loadLearningProgress` and any future caller.

### Notifications

Push flows that resolve an app id per opportunity (`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity`, used
by session-endpoint notifications in `FirebaseMessagingUtil`) must handle a job with no apps without
crashing.

## Builder's discretion

- Exact name and form of the type predicate and the default value constant.
- Whether app-launch branching lives in `BaseConnectFragment.launchApp` or in each CTA handler.
- CTA label strings for Claim and messaging. Use `dev-utils:add-mobile-string` for new strings.
- Test structure, following AGENTS.md: unit tests for parsing, status, and migration; Robolectric UI
  tests for Intro claim → Delivery Home and the messaging CTA.
- Updating `docs/connect/` with a short note on the messaging delivery type.

# PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities

## Intent

Connect is adding a new kind of opportunity in which delivery happens through PersonalID messaging
instead of a CommCare deliver app. These opportunities never have a deliver app. They may or may not
have a learn app:

- **With a learn app:** learning works as today. After claiming, the worker goes to Delivery Home,
  whose CTA opens messaging instead of a deliver app.
- **Without a learn app:** the worker reads Intro, claims from Intro, and goes straight to Delivery
  Home with the messaging CTA.

Today the mobile app assumes every opportunity has both apps. Parsing, storage, status derivation,
and most Connect screens dereference `learnAppInfo` / `deliveryAppInfo` unconditionally, so an
opportunity without them either fails to parse or crashes.

## Goals

- Opportunities with `delivery_type = "personalid_messaging"` parse, store, and display without
  crashing, with or without a learn app.
- Without a learn app: job list → Intro → **Claim** on Intro → DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the
  messaging CTA.
- With a learn app: job list → Intro → start learning → learn app → learn progress → claim →
  DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the messaging CTA.
- The status stays DELIVERING across syncs after claim.
- Existing learn/deliver opportunities behave exactly as today.

## Non-goals

- Opening a specific messaging channel. The server will later add a channel id to the opportunity
  config; until then the CTA opens the messaging channel list.
- Server-driven opportunity status. Status remains derived on the device.
- Server changes (the claim endpoint accepting a claim with no learning when there is no learn app,
  sending `delivery_type`). These are prerequisites owned by the server team.

## Server contract

On the opportunity list API, for a PersonalID messaging opportunity:

- `delivery_type`: new string field. `"personalid_messaging"` marks this type. Absent or any other
  value means the existing learn/deliver type (older servers, existing cached jobs).
- `deliver_app`: always `null`.
- `learn_app`: an app object, or `null` when the opportunity has no learn app.
- `learn_progress`: still present; parsed as today.

Other APIs:

- Learn progress API: the client must never call it for a job whose `learnAppInfo` is null.
- Claim API: called from Intro when there is no learn app, and from learn progress (as today) when
  there is one. Without a learn app, the server accepts the claim with no learning completed.
- Delivery progress, deliveries, and payments APIs: unchanged.

## Design

### Data model and storage

- Add a persisted `deliveryType` field to `ConnectJobRecord` (`delivery_type`). Branches use two
  checks on the record:
  - **PersonalID messaging delivery** (`deliveryType == "personalid_messaging"`): governs everything
    on the delivery side (deliver app, Delivery Home CTA, tasks).
  - **Has learn app** (`learnAppInfo != null`): governs everything on the learn side (Intro learn
    cards, start learning vs. claim, learn progress API, revisit learning).
- Bump `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` (currently 30), add the `ConnectJobRecordV<N>` snapshot, and add an
  upgrade step in `ConnectDatabaseUpgrader` that backfills existing rows with the default type.
  Prior migrations that targeted `ConnectJobRecord.class` must be retargeted to the new snapshot,
  following the existing V2…V21 pattern.
- `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson`:
  - PersonalID messaging job: `learn_app` is nullable. `deliver_app` is ignored and the deliver app
    record is always null, even if the server sends one. *(Our call.)*
  - Any other job: a null or missing `learn_app` or `deliver_app` is rejected as malformed (throws,
    so `ConnectOpportunitiesParser` skips the job as it does other bad entries). This keeps
    learn/deliver paths free of null guards. *(Our call.)*
- `JobStoreManager` (store and delete paths, learn module writes) and `ConnectJobUtils`
  (`getAppIdForOpportunity`) skip absent app records instead of dereferencing them.

### Status

Status is set locally in four places:

| Where | What it does | PersonalID messaging change |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson` | Derives AVAILABLE / LEARNING / DELIVERING from learn progress and `claim`. | New branch, below. |
| `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` | Keeps the stored status if it is further along than the parsed one; marks newly seen AVAILABLE jobs AVAILABLE_NEW. | None. |
| `ConnectJobIntroFragment` start-learning success | Sets LEARNING. | Unchanged with a learn app; not reached without one. |
| `ConnectRepository.claimJob` success | Sets DELIVERING. | None; both claim entry points reuse it. |

`fromJson` branch for PersonalID messaging jobs:

1. `claim` present → DELIVERING.
2. Otherwise, has a learn app and learn progress > 0 → LEARNING.
3. Otherwise → AVAILABLE.

Without a learn app the job never enters LEARNING. The claim rule is needed because the
no-regression rule in `storeOrUpdateJob` only protects a device that recorded the claim locally. A
fresh install, a second device, or a claim made outside this device would otherwise derive
AVAILABLE and show Intro for a claimed job.

`passedAssessment()` reads `learnAppInfo.passingScore`, so it must not run for jobs without a learn
app.

### Screens

| Screen | With learn app | Without learn app |
|---|---|---|
| Job list (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment`) | Learning entries as today. Delivering entries skip the deliver-app install check and last-accessed lookup. | No app install checks or last-accessed lookups. |
| Intro (`ConnectJobIntroFragment`) | As today: learn cards shown, CTA starts learning. | Learn cards dropped entirely. CTA claims the job, then navigates to Delivery Home. |
| Learn progress (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView`) | Claim success always navigates to Delivery Home; never launches a deliver app. The learn-complete CTA uses the "go to delivery" label, never the download-app label. | Not reached. |
| Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`) | CTA opens messaging via `ConnectNavHelper.goToMessaging` (no channel id for now). No deliver-app install checks. `loadLearningProgress` runs as today. | Same, but `loadLearningProgress` is skipped. |
| Delivery dashboard / more | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" shown as today. | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" hidden. |
| `ConnectActivity.handleInfoRedirect` | As today. | A non-delivering job routes to Intro, not the learn progress screen. |

For jobs without a learn app, Intro needs claim handling (loading, error, success). It currently
lives only in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`, so Intro's ViewModel needs the same handling.

Where job list cards would read description and organization from an app record that is absent,
they read them from the job record and use the existing card styles. No new card design. *(Our
call.)*

### Tasks

PersonalID messaging jobs can have pending tasks. Opening one goes through
`ConnectTaskPresenter.open` from the dashboard and More tabs:

- **Conversation task** (`isOCSConversation`): unchanged. Opens messaging on the task's channel.
- **Any other task**: shows an error toast, "No action found for the task", instead of launching
  the deliver app. No navigation.
- The More tab's pending-task badge is unchanged.

**Delivery Home CTA enablement.** Today's rule
(`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment.updateCtaBarEnabled`) is: the CTA is disabled only when the deliver
app is installed **and** at least one task is pending. Otherwise it is enabled.

For PersonalID messaging jobs, the messaging CTA counts as an installed deliver app: **the CTA is
disabled while any task is pending, and enabled otherwise.** Accepted risk: a pending
non-conversation task blocks the CTA, and tapping it only shows the toast, so the worker stays
blocked until the server clears the task.

### Learn progress API guard

Guard inside `ConnectRepository.getLearningProgress`: if `learnAppInfo` is null, don't make the call.
This covers Delivery Home's `loadLearningProgress` and any future caller.

### Notifications

`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity` (used by session-endpoint notifications in
`FirebaseMessagingUtil`) returns no app id when the requested app is absent: always for delivery
status, and for learn status when there is no learn app. The caller drops the notification as it
already does when the app id can't be resolved.

## Builder's discretion

- Exact names of the two checks and the delivery type constant.
- Whether app-launch branching lives in `BaseConnectFragment.launchApp` or in each CTA handler.
- CTA label strings for Claim and messaging. Use `dev-utils:add-mobile-string` for new strings.
- Test structure, following AGENTS.md: unit tests for parsing (both variants), status, and
  migration; Robolectric UI tests for Intro claim → Delivery Home, learn-complete claim → Delivery
  Home, and the messaging CTA.
- Updating `docs/connect/` with a short note on the PersonalID messaging delivery type.

content.text:
When `learnAppInfo` is null, there are no learn modules to write. The server only sends modules inside the `learn_app` object. [Certain] `ConnectAppRecord.fromJson` (`ConnectAppRecord.java:89-94`) builds the module list from `learn_app.learn_modules`. `learn_progress` carries only the counts (`total_modules`, `completed_modules`). So a `null` `learn_app` means the server sent zero modules.

Your intent still works: the stored modules should match what the server sent. For a null `learnAppInfo`, that means treating the incoming module list as empty, not skipping the module step. `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateLearnModules` (`:296-324`) then:
- deletes any modules stored for the job, which matters if an opportunity loses its learn app after the device has already synced it, and
- writes nothing.

I've updated the doc to say this. The rule for the app records themselves is unchanged: nothing is written or deleted for a null app.
